Character Index - J[]

J.A.[]

Appearances: Fear Itself: The Home Front #1

J.A. was an elderly retired man from Broxton who found himself in financial difficulties and was forced to work as a waiter in a diner in the town, having to serve the multitude of tourists who visited Broxton to see the Asgardians.[1]

J.B.[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #82, Daredevil #165

JB was a TV network executive who accepted Spider-Man's offer to appear on one of his late-night talk shows.[2]
Some time later, JB attended a Glenn Industries board meeting.[3]

J.C.[]

Appearances: Spider-Man #84

J.C. was a friend of Devon Lewis.[4]

J.D.[]

Appearances: Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #1, Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #2, Ghost Rider (Vol. 3) #3

J.D. he was a member of the Cypress Pool Jokers youth gang in Brooklyn. He was one of the three who hid one of the three canisters stolen from the Kingpin and hidden in a mausoleum in Cypress Hills Cemetery.[5]

J.G.[]

Appearances: Tales of Suspense #37

Joe's employer and supervisor. J.G. reprimanded Joe after public complaints arose concerning the giant paper-mâché monster used to promote a motion picture, considering the campaign a failure despite its unintended cosmic consequences.[5]

Jack[]

Appearances: Marvel Mystery Comics #28

Two sailors, Jack and Slim, were caught in a storm but survived, only to find themselves marooned in the Sargasso Sea, among a myriad of ships stranded for a long time in that stretch of water known as the "Sea of ​​Doomed Ships." But among all those wrecks, one ship remained intact. It was, in fact, a German spy ship exploiting its location and superstition to transmit the movements of Allied forces to the Fatherland. Jack and Slim were captured, tied up, and thrown into a cabin, but they managed to free themselves and, taking advantage of the night hours and the sleeping guards, managed to radio a nearby destroyer, thus capturing the German crew.[6]

Appearances: Marvel Tales #110

An apartment owner, decides to commit arson in order to get rid of an unwanted property so he figures that if he calls the fire department from the top floor of the burning building, no one will accuse him of setting the fire. He figures out how long that it should take the fire truck to respond to his phone call from the top floor and then lights a fire on the ground floor. He rushes up the stairs to the pay phone on the top floor and remembers that he doesn't have any coins.[7]

Appearances: Captain America #170

Jack was murdered by Moonstone in a small Midwestern university.[8]

Appearances: Nova #1

Jack was a classmate of Richard Rider at Harry S. Truman High School and played for the same basketball team. Jack blamed Rider for having missed aa block, causing their team to lose the game.[9]

Appearances: Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #43, Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #47, Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #48

Jack, Manny e Moe were Belladonna's henchmen. They participated in the various raids which, disguised as fashion design thefts, were put in place to discredit and ruin Roderick Kingsley.[10][11]
After tricking Spider-Man into going to Roderick Kingsley, Belladonna called Jack by phone telling him to get the boys together as that would be the big payoff. During the final showdown between Belladonna and her gang against Spider-Man, they were all easily defeated by the hero and handed over to the police.[12]

Appearances: Web of Spider-Man #4

Jack was a security personnel that worked at a facility that kept Doctor Octopus' Tentacles while he was being treated at the South Brooklyn Psychiatric Facility. His partner was observing them thrash in their holding room and Jack was eating a sandwich nonchalantly and unconcerned.[13]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #383

Jack was acting as Gregor in Metamorphosis on Broadway with Nadia Dornova, when he suddenly disappeared in thin air.[14]

Appearances: Web of Spider-Man #110

Only eight miles outside Lubbock, Jack and Rog noticed a vehicle in trouble. While they were investigating the scene, the Lizard slithered on board of their truck. The two truckers, who were working for 'Louisiana Leathers', were allegedly slaughtered by the villain near the Mississippi border.[15]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #6

Jack and his partner were caught by Spider-Man after they tried to rob a church collection box at gunpoint.[16]

Appearances: Avengers (Vol. 3) #21

Jack was a member of the troops sent by the United Nations as part of Operation Metalstorm to free Slorenia from Ultron.[17]

Appearances: Captain America (Vol. 4) #1

Jack witnessed a terrorist attack in Centerville on Easter Sunday.[18]

Appearances: Haunt of Horror: Lovecraft #1

Jack and his companion Yagar went an expedition to find his lost father. After finding a trinket, Jack experienced a vision of events that took place centuries ago where Jack's ancestor led a group of warriors to kill many innocent people, including a witch who cursed the warrior's family line until the end of time. After coming out of the vision, Jack turned to see Yagar bearing the face of the witch woman killed so long ago. The woman smiled and repeated her original curse, at which point Jack turned into a skeleton and died.[19]

Appearances: Invincible Iron Man (Vol. 2) #10

Jack was among the reporters who came to the H.A.M.M.E.R. press conference.[20]

Appearances: Fear Itself: The Home Front #2, Fear Itself: The Home Front #3, Fear Itself: The Home Front #7

Jack was a citizen of Stamford who participated in the posse who captured Speedball for wanting to execute him by suffocating him with a plastic bag,[21] until the intervention of Miriam Sharpe, and when Jack was surprised that she of all people took the defense against their kind, Miriam retorted in rhyme, making fun of the kind.[22]
Though frightened, Jack and the other Stamford residents fought back at the onslaught of the Sisters of Sin.[23]

Appearances: Storm (Vol. 3) #6

Jack was the bodyguard of a United States senator who attacked Storm.[24]

Jackie[]

Appearances: Black Panther #14, Black Panther #15

A member of the Harlem gang the Thunderbolts, Jackie used the Sonic Disruptor against the Black Panther while he was under Klaw's influence.[25]
After being defeated by the Avengers, Jackie was arrested by the police.[26]

Appearances: Untold Tales of Spider-Man: Strange Encounters #1

Jackie and Mose were robbing the Chicago Museum of Antiquities when Jackie was hypnotized by an artifact that forced him to break the case containing it and take it for himself. The artifact was the mystical Lantern of Lantarr and both of them, under its influence, carried out kidnappings in New York City for Baron Mordo, until he transformed them into demonic forms.[27]

Appearances: X-Men/Spider-Man #1

Jackie was a talk show host who invited J. Jonah Jameson and Kraven the Hunter onto her show.[28]

Appearances: Captain Marvel (Vol. 7) #3

Jackie complained to George Howard that women were excluded from the astronaut program, and when Howard pointed out that entry into the program required military jet experience, Jackie pointed out that women were not allowed to fly jets.[29]

Jackson[]

Appearances: Avengers #178

Mr. Jackson, along with other three crime bosses, had a meeting with the Manipulator to whom he wanted to sell his services, demonstrating how he could manipulate the Beast, and sure that he could manipulate all the Avengers. After obtaining the money from the bosses, however, he put them under his control and handed them over to two government agents.[30]

Appearances: Peter Parker, The Spectacular Spider-Man #106

Jackson was one of Vince Granetti's henchmen and tried to shoot the Wasp when a Quinjet appeared on the tracks in front of a train carrying drugs. Him and his men succeeded in nearly destroying the Quinjet but failed to recover the Wasp who had been hiding and attacked thereafter.[31]

Appearances: Web of Spider-Man #27

Jackson was Lee Camino's limousine driver. Leaving the courthouse after being acquitted of the murder charge against Anthony Delandri, Camino got into the limousine and noticed Headhunter in the crowd. Terrified, he yelled at Jackson to drive off immediately and not stop until he reached his home.[32]

Appearances: Spider-Man #45

Jackson was one of the men sent by Frank Cortese to protect Mister C. He and his squad were all defeated by Spider-Man in Central Park.[33]

Mentions: Amazing Fantasy #16

Jackson was the bill collector who took care of Maxie Shiffman's debts. After another phone call to Shiffman to get paid, Maxie asked him for another week since he had Spider-Man as a client.[34]

Appearances: Ultimate Invasion #1

Jackson was a mercenary who filled in for the late Keith Conrad as part of a squad assembled by Randall West to get to the Maker within the Damage Control Remote Prison 42 inside the Blaakguard Building in Chicago.

Once the team made contact with their secret employer, the Maker used a device that merged the four mercenaries and transfigured them into a near-catatonic duplicate of himself. The gestalt decoy stayed in its place until Mister Fantastic investigated the cell, at which point it melted into a puddle after taunting him.[35]

Jacob[]

Appearances: 4 #5, 4 #6, 4 #7

Jacob and Jeff were filmmakers who were making a documentary about the Jersey Devil (Cryptid).[36]
They approached and entered an alien spaceship.[37]
They both were eventually rescued by the Fantastic Four.[38]

Jacques[]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #273

Mentions: Incredible Hulk #274

Pierre and Jacques were two Canadian loggers, and as they were about to cut down some trees Pierre jokingly told Jacques if he could imagine it if he could cut down all the trees with one blow, and Jacques replied that he must be a real blowhard. Both of them did not imagine that the Hulk was listening to them, and making a joke he blew him for real toward the trees while Pierre did it for pretend, in effect felling the trees in the forest thus taking the trouble of felling them away from the loggers.[39]

Appearances: Power Man and Iron Fist #117

Jacques was a wino who along with his fellow wino saw Maxine Walters and Danny Rand descending into an abandoned subway tunnel. They sought to protect Maxine from Danny whom they assumed was a Martian because of the protective suit he was forced to wear after being exposed to a nuclear blast.[40] John Lumus then appeared and killed the winos on his quest to take out Maxine Walters.[41]

Appearances: Immortal Iron Fist #2

Jacques fought in Fort Souville with Orson Randall.[42]

Jacquesmon[]

Mentions: Punisher (Vol. 2) #58

Leader of the Red Hares. He assigned Miltion Melchior to attend the meeting between his operative Jacques Delacroix and George Wong, the representative of the Kingpin, and provided Melchior with a letter to be read during the proceedings.[43]

Jacquet[]

Appearances: Marvels #1

Mrs. Jacquet was the mother of Doris Jacquet and mother-in-law of Phil Sheldon. She was very excited about the marriage between her daughter and Phil.[44]

Jakes[]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 2) #11

Jakes was Burt Corrigan's chauffeur.[45]

Jaleel[]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 3) #7

Jaleel was one of the students from the Cresskill School for the Blind who were rescued by Matthew Murdock when their bus crashed during a snowstorm in the Catskill Mountains.[46]

Jaime[]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 2) #36

Jaime was a falangist kid who was taken prisoner by Eric Blair.[47]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 2) #116, Daredevil (Vol. 2) #500

Jaime was the son of Marta, a woman who met and started a relationship with Wilson Fisk when he tried to start a new life in Spain. Fisk became a father figure for Jaime and his sister Adriana, who called him "Uncle Wheelie". However, Jamie and the rest of his family were slaughtered by the Hand and Lady Bullseye.[48]

Jamaal[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #548

Jamaal was a taxi cab driver who took Spider-Man to Battery Park.[49]

Jamal[]

Appearances: Fantastic Four (Vol. 6) #29

Jamal was a neighbor of Sky in the Soho neighborhood.[50]

Jamar[]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 8) #2

Jamar was a gangster confronted by the Punisher.[51]

Jan[]

Appearances: Fantastic Four #232

Jan gave the Thing a scuba tank when he crashed into the sporting goods store where she was working, allowing him to breathe during a fight against a water elemental sent by Diablo. Jan was then trapped by the same water elemental and was in turn rescued by the Thing.[52]

Appearances: New X-Men Annual #2001

Jan was a U-Man who attended John Sublime's public event to highlight the "Third Species".[53]

Jane[]

Mentions: Avengers #119

A participant in the annual Rutland Halloween parade, insisted on getting an autograph from the Scarlet Witch and the Vision and despite the Scarlet Witch's refusal saying that they wanted to be left alone, the man, ironically calling her Greta Garbo, told her that he had promised it to his wife Jane, infuriating Wanda who used her hex powers to push him away.[54]

Appearances: Amazing Fantasy (Vol. 2) #13, Amazing Fantasy (Vol. 2) #14

Jane was the twin sister of the criminal known as Vegas.[55]
She was a scientist who used to work with Dr. Heisenberg.[56]

Appearances: Avenging Spider-Man #7

Jane was a colleague of Jennifer Walters at the law firm. During the opening of an Ancient Egypt exhibit that the law firm was sponsoring, Jane scolded Jennifer for introducing herself as She-Hulk, telling her that Jennifer Walters worked for the law firm, not She-Hulk, and that she didn't smell good.[57]

Appearances: Marvel 75th Anniversary Celebration #1

Jane was saved by fireman David Walker during the Human Torch's first appearance in New York City. 75 years later, Jane requested Jessica Jones's assistance in finding Walker, in order to properly thank him for saving her life.[58]

Janelle[]

Appearances: Daredevil Annual #7

Janelle was criminal Richard Furman's associate, and she was privy of details of Furman's illegal deals with corrupt NYPD detective Hobbes.[59]

Janet[]

Appearances: Daredevil #91, Daredevil #95, Daredevil #97, Daredevil #101, and Daredevil #107

Janet worked in San Francisco for the Law Office of Broderick, Sloan, and Cranston and would continue working for the firm after Cranston's death.[60] Janet was still working at the the law office when Matt Murdock was made a partner.[61]

Appearances: Haunt of Horror (Vol. 2) #2

Janet suffered physical violence from her husband soon after her mother, who lived with them, died. One evening, returning to his house drunk, her husband violently hit her with one objects, killing her, after which he himself was killed by their son Jimmy, advised to him, according to him, by the corpse of her grandmother.[62]

Appearances: Darkhawk #3

Janet was a friend and schoolmate of Chris Powell's. She was the girlfriend of Bob, another friend of Chris's, and a photography enthusiast. [63]

Appearances: Sensational She-Hulk #52

Janet was Greg Hallerhand's Personal Assistant at CBC.[64]

Appearances: Marvel Double Shot #4

Janet and her friend Davy were saved by Doctor Strange from the Bottle Imp.[65]

Janey[]

Appearances: Eternals Annual #1

Janey was saved by Karkas from Attila the Hun.[66]

Appearances: Marvel Two-In-One #98

Janey and Brad were two kids who encountered the Thing along with Franklin Richards in an Arcade. When Brad saw it she mistook it for "Evil Otto", but Janey corrected him that that was just a video game character, but she wasn't entirely sure.[67]

Appearances: Thunderbolts #4

In a television station near the Adirondack Mountains, Janey decided to send to her network a remote broadcast from the Thunderbolts, while they were fighting Arnim Zola inside Doctor Doom's Castle.[68]

Jangles[]

Appearances: Captain America #170 & Captain America #171

Jangles was one of Stoneface's henchmen.[8]
He was confronted by the Black Panther and Falcon.[69]

Janice[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #279

Janice was a fashion model working for Kingsley Ltd.[70]

Appearances: Emma Frost #6

Janice was an interior designer who advised how to furnish the Frost House in preparation for a party hosted by Winston.[71]

Appearances: Emma Frost #15

Janice was a homeless woman from whom Astrid Bloom read her mind to discover that she found herself living on the street when her husband died.[72]

Appearances: Thunderbolts (Vol. 2) #168

Janice was a pawn of Mister Fear. Luke Cage was made to believe he killed her due to visions caused by Mister Fear's fear gas. However, Cage soon discovered that Janice had been poisoned and not killed by him.[73]

Janie[]

Appearances: Totally Awesome Hulk #7

Janie was a hospital receptionist from Las Vegas who met Bruce Banner.[74]

Janos[]

Appearances: Havok and Wolverine - Meltdown # 3

Janos escorted Havok and Scarlett across the Soviet border in the western Carpathian Mountains.[75]

Janssen[]

Appearances: Avengers (Vol. 3) #0

Doctor Janssen's hospital was attacked, and she survived barely long enough to tell Wonder Man that his brother, the Grim Reaper, had been attacked and kidnapped by robots.[76]

Jarret[]

Appearances: Black Widow (Vol. 2) #2

Jarret was a security guard at the New York Museum of Natural History who attempted to arrest Yelena Belova, who was led by SHIELD to believe she was Natasha Romanov, after killing what appeared to be Yelena Belova, but was taken hostage by her for later run away.[77]

Jasmine[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #332

Jasmine was a baby girl who was taking a carriage ride with her parents in Central Park when the carriage that was crossing a small bridge was hit by a car thrown by Venom who wanted to hit Spider-Man. The carriage overturned and the baby was thrown out of the carriage and fell into the stretch of water under the bridge, but surprisingly it was Venom himself who saved her by pulling her out of the water and handing her over to her parents.[78]

Jason[]

Appearances: West Coast Avengers #3

Jason was a looter arrested by the West Coast Avengers.[79]

Appearances: Marvel Super-Heroes (Vol. 2) #4

Jason was Annie's son.[80]

Appearances: Fantastic Four (Vol. 3) #560, Fantastic Four (Vol. 3) #563, Fantastic Four (Vol. 3) #566

Jason was Debbie Green's ex-boyfriend.[81] He was threatened live on television by the Thing.[82]

Appearances: Marvel Fanfare #60

Jason was freed from the McCarthy Medical Treatment Center by the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants.[83]

Appearances: Siege #2

Jason helped Maria Hill and Thor during the Siege of Asgard.[84]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 6) #30

Jason was Wilson Fisk's personal trainer who had a dissertation with Fisk during a training session about his unusual good mood.[85]

Appearances: Uncanny X-Men #437

Jason was a gas station attendant in Kentucky when Jeb Guthrie used his powers on Abe Cabot. He hit Jeb on the back of the head with a crowbar and made a racist remark to black people and mutants, causing Raymond Holder Jr. (Earth-616) to flip the boy holding him over his shoulder, colliding with Jason. When Jason got to his feet, he threw the crowbar at Jeb, but Jeb used his powers to deflect it, accidentally causing a car to explode.[86]

Jasper[]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #180

Jasper was renowned throughout the county for his stubbornness and hair-trigger temper.[87]

Appearances: Marvel Graphic Novel: The Amazing Spider-Man: Hooky

Jasper with his two partners, Kenny and Duke were trying to break into a warehouse in a clumsy way and also started arguing with each other, when Spider-Man arrived and pointed out their clumsiness by calling them Curly, Larry and Moe and easily knocking them out and handing them over to the police.[88]

Appearances: Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #1-4 & 13

Jasper and Tierra were two twin Under-Yorker children whose mother, Leilani, hid in the laundry basket of her neighbor, Peter Parker, so that Spider-Man could protect them.[89]

Jassim[]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 3) #64

Jassim was one of Mordad's men.[90]

Jasta[]

Appearances: Punisher: In the Blood #1

Warden Jasta was the warden of the Temple prison, where the Hood's dwarf aide, Jaten, was incarcerated. After infiltrating the prison to obtain information about the Hood from Jaten, the Punisher telephoned Warden Jasta, telling him that a bomb had been planted in his prison and that he only had time to evacuate the prison staff, not the inmates.[91]

Javi[]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 3) #7

Javi was one of the students from the Cresskill School for the Blind who were rescued by Matthew Murdock when their bus crashed during a snowstorm in the Catskill Mountains.[46]

Javier[]

Appearances: Daredevil: Reborn #4

Javier was a member of the Cartels of Calavera. He and another member of the Cartels were on guard and debated about the power of calavera and how it gave him nightmares when Matt Murdock broke in and hit him stunned.[92]

Appearances: X-Men Unlimited Infinity Comic #36

Javier was a Mexican boy who, together with his friends Gabi and Miguel, found a deep hole and outside what remained of the pupal state of one of Maggott's endosymbiotes and were terrified when they saw the slug grown to gigantic size.[93]

Jaxon[]

Appearances: Alpha Flight #12

Jerry Jaxon's ex-wife was also the daughter of his former boss at Am-Can Corporation. When Jerry was fired following the betrayal, according to her, by James Hudson who had taken away the exploratory super-costume, on returning home she abandoned him also taking away her two little children.[94]

Appearances: Alpha Flight #12

Jerry Jaxon's son, was taken away from his wife when she abandoned him following his firing from Am-Can Corporation.[94]

Appearances: Alpha Flight #12

Jerry Jaxon's little daughter was taken away from his wife when she abandoned him following his dismissal from Am-Can Corporation.[94]

Jay[]

Appearances: Marvels #2

A reporter for the Daily Globe, Jay, and his colleague Gavin were told by Barney Bushkin to cover the Sentinels' story.[95]

Appearances: Black Widow (Vol. 3) #1

Jay was crippled by the Black Widow after he tried to harass Sally Anne Carter.[96]

Appearances: Dark Reign: Young Avengers #1

Jay was a robber who confronted the Young Masters during one of their self-recorded "heroic acts". However, he was brutally killed by Big Zero, who simply grew up in size and stomped on him.[97]

Jayden[]

Appearances: Venom/Carnage Infinity Comic #3

Jayden was the birthday girl at a bachelorette party in Las Vegas during the clash between Venom and Carnage with the latter causing a blackout, ruining the party, and her complaining that she would settle for a pizza and a movie night.[98]

Jaz[]

Appearances: Daken: Dark Wolverine #5, Daken: Dark Wolverine #6, Daken: Dark Wolverine #7

Jaz was a woman in the service of Tyger Tiger and was among those who dealt with the release of the boys and girls held as sexual slaves by Petrus.[99]
Jaz pretended to be condescending with a corrupt banker in order to slip him a drug that caused symptoms similar to a heart attack, a ploy designed by Tyger Tiger to appropriate the banker's briefcase.[100]
Jaz was later killed by Daken so that Tyger could not manage his men.[101]

Jean[]

Appearances: Menace #9

Jean was the butler of the famous and arrogant music critic Georges Descourtes, always ready to satisfy the whims of his hateful master.[102]

Appearances: Journey Into Mystery #31

Detective Dave regretted not marrying his old girlfriend Jean instead of his current wife Madge who was also his boss's daughter.[103]

Appearances: Iron Man (Vol. 3) #8

Jean was a flower seller from Paris who knew Yvette Avril.[104]

Appearances: Ironheart #2

Mr. Jean was the owner of a shop in Boston. He was helped by Ironheart to oppose a further request for extortion by a gang of criminals, and despite the heroine's intervention, he felt resigned to yield to the demands of the criminals.[105]

Jean-Pierre[]

Appearances: Doctor Strange (Vol. 2) #78

Jean-Pierre was a teenager who was stopped by Cloak from taking Ecstasy's drug.[106]

Jeanette[]

Appearances: Zombie #4; Zombie #5

Jeanette was a friend of Phillip Bliss.[107] She witnessed Steve Bergen and Gene Gretch follow him home.[108]

Appearances: Marvel Graphic Novel: Wolverine: Bloodlust

Jeanette and her family were killed by Neuri rebels.[109]

Jeanie[]

Appearances: Captain America (Vol. 5) #614

Jeanie is an overweight, married, middle-aged woman.[110]

Jeanne[]

Appearances: Tales of Suspense #40

Jeanne was a romantic interest of Tony Stark when he first became Iron Man. She told Tony that she wished he would come to Monte Carlo more often, so she could see more of him.[111]

Jeb[]

Appearances: Man-Thing #17

Jeb was the caretaker of Citrusvilles sewage treatment plant. When Orville Latimer arrived with the apparently dead body of the Man-Thing intending to dispose of it in the facility, Jeb enthusiastically supported the idea, though he informed Latimer that authorization from the mayor would first be required.[112]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 3) #63

In 1921, Jeb was confronted and defeated by Logan in Kansas City.[113]

Jed[]

Appearances: Elektra #2

Jed and his gang were attacked by the Snakeroot.[114]

Appearances: X-Man #10

Jed was a boy who met Nate Grey at the diner in Skunk Hollow, North Carolina, and like everyone else at the diner, they were terrified when they discovered Nate was a mutant.[115]

Jeeves[]

Appearances: Spectacular Spider-Man #257

Jeeves was one of the many people who helped Peter and Mary Jane Watson-Parker move into their Bedford Tower apartment.[116]

Jeff[]

Appearances: Iron Man #48

Jeff and his partner Frank stopped Tony Stark and warned him about the local speed laws.[117]

Appearances: Journey Into Mystery #56

After mocking the local tales of a haunted lighthouse with his friends, John finds himself sheltering inside it after his fishing boat capsizes during a storm. He searches the lighthouse from top to bottom but finds no evidence of "haunting" until just before midnight when the main light is turned on revealing a mysterious ship coming towards the lighthouse. The ship has a strange glow and lowers several smaller boats containing ghosts into the water. John hides as the ghosts come through the walls and discuss their plans. At one point the ghosts seem to feel his presence but dismiss the feeling as they are sure none of the locals would dare risk being killed by the ghosts. In the morning, John is telling his friends of his ordeal. They laugh at him until he shows them a life-preserver from the "Flying Dutchmen", left behind by the dead sailors.[316]

Appearances: Tales to Astonish #11

When his son Billy went missing in the swamp, John went out to try and find him. John found his son but then Monstrom appeared and the family fled to town when bullets didn't stop it.[317]

Appearances: Tales to Astonish #15

While John and Derek were on a hunting expedition in Africa they came into possession of a medallion which depicted a mastodon. Derek believed the find meant they were close to the presence of a legendary elephant graveyard where the two could find immense riches of ivory. They started their search, spotting a nearby elephant and chose to follow it. They followed the elephant to a glowing forest where the guides ran off in fear while Derek was seized by greed, choosing to shoot John in one leg to appropriate all the ivory he would find for himself. Fortunately one of the African guides, Monga, heard the gunshot and returned to John's side bringing him to safety. John never learned Derek's fate but was glad he didn't accompany him further as some things are better left undiscovered.[318]

Appearances: Tales of Suspense #23

John and his wife Martha gave up their business to retire to Florida. There they helped an alien to return to his ship and to thank them for their kindness, the alien bathed them (without their knowledge) with the waters of the swamp, which were the fountain of youth. John and Martha lost some memory and they both found themselves rejuvenated, not remembering that they had been elderly and that they had met the alien.[319]

When he wakes the boy in the dead of night, the boy is frightened and refuses to be cowed into submission so the regent falls back upon his threat to use his black magic to transform the prince into a toad. However, the regent's spell backfires on him and the prince laughs at his new toad companion saying that "you forgot that fairy tales always have happy endings."[320]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 5) #78

Operator Johnson belonged to the intervention team of the Beyond Corporation who intervened to rescue Spider-Man at the request of the Langston artificial intelligence after the assault by Morbius.[374]

Jolel[]

Appearances: X-Factor #76

Jolel was a staunch supporter of Farnoq Dahn, and meeting Wolfsbane stunned after being thrown away by the Hulk, he took her prisoner while waiting for Dahn's men to take her away. During their captivity, Rahne and Jolel had a heated discussion about their beliefs. When Rahne was about to flee, Jolel's sister Sandah helped her by hitting Jolel with a bottle. When Jolel recovered from her he killed her sister with a knife infuriating Wolfsbane who in return killed Jolel.[375]

Jolene[]

Appearances: Amazing Fantasy #1000

Jolene untied Arnulfa Gonzales, who had been confined to her bed after one of her fits, as a fire had developed in the hospital where she had been admitted. Jolene told Arnulfa that they had to escape but as soon as she left Arnulfa's room, she Jolene was engulfed in flames and perished.[376]

Jomo[]

Appearances: Moon Knight (Vol. 2) #6

Jomo was one of Mother White's sons and part of her drug operation. When they took on Moon Knight, he was killed when Mother White blew up their base of operations by accident when shooting at Moon Knight and hitting a gas main.[377]

Jon[]

Appearances: Civil War: The Initiative #1

Jon was the closest friend of Michael Pointer during their years living in the small town of North Pole, Alaska. His life came to a tragic end when the community was annihilated in a catastrophic explosion caused by the mutant energies manipulated by Xorn. Those energies converged uncontrollably within Michael, triggering the blast that destroyed the town and claimed Jon among its many victims.[378]

Jonah[]

Appearances: Two-Gun Kid #89

Jonah is a resident of Tombstone.[379]

Appearances: Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #8, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #9, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #10, Ms. Marvel (Vol. 4) #11

Jonah studied criminal justice at Rutgers. He was one of the volunteers who were put together in the Carol Cadets by Becky St. Jude to put Ulysses' knowledge to good use.[380]

Jonas[]

Appearances: Uncanny Tales #32

Mr. Jonas was the owner of a store where janitor Ned Carter worked. Jonas fired Carter because he didn't show up for work because he was full-time working on creating a robot that would sweep the floors for him. After several attempts, Carter managed to create a robot capable of sweeping the floor but not moving beyond just sweeping movements. Considering it a further failure, he surrendered to the evidence by destroying the robot and asking Mr. Jonas to get him back to work.[381]

Jonathan[]

Appearances: Amazing Fantasy #1000

Jonathan was a friend of Neil Gaiman. When Neil went to New York, Jonathan managed to get Neil to meet Steve Ditko with whom he corresponded.[376]

Jonson[]

Appearances: Untold Tales of Spider-Man #25

Jonson was one of Crime-Master's henchmen assigned to drive the mobile van that Crime-Master used to control the attempted theft of the Seismic Ray Device from the Empire State University labs. When he attempted to blow up the Multi-Environmental Testing Chamber, in which Spider-Man and Green Goblin were trapped, he destroyed the Chamber's controls, then fled in the van, ordering Jonson to return to headquarters as they were finished there.[382]

Joon[]

Appearances: Emma Frost #2, Emma Frost #3

Joon was a classmate of Emma Frost at Snow Valley School for Girls and from whom she obtained the answers for her midterm exams by reading her mind unconsciously not yet knowing she was a telepathic mutant.[383]
Joon later asked Emma if she used ginseng to improve her intellectual performance.[384]

Appearances: Elektra: Black, White & Blood #2

Joon was a professional escort in Madripoor, of whom a crime boss Cesare thought she was carrying his son. When Cesare learned that Joon was going to terminate her pregnancy he decided to intervene, but to help Joon intervened Elektra, as a favor for Logan. However, who eliminated Cesare was Joon herself who shot Cesare while fighting with Elektra killing him and with his death she decided to carry on the pregnancy, as her son was not his but Ryan's.[385]

Jordan[]

Appearances: Tales to Astonish #40

Mrs. Jordan was the mother of Tommy Jordan, a boy who, due to a series of fortuitous events, found himself in an alternative reality practically identical to theirs where a family lived in which the mother was an identical copy of Tommy's mother.[386]

Appearances: Magneto: Not a Hero #2 & Magneto: Not a Hero #3

Jordan was Christopher Bach's bodyguard.[387][388]

Jordon[]

Appearances: Marvel Mystery Comics #26

Mr. Jordon was the Editor of the Globe Press newspaper. He assigned some reporters to investigate the ghost mine after Terry Vance tipped off what he thought was going on there.[389]

Jorge[]

Appearances: Fantastic Four #277

Jorge was the apartment manager at Alicia Masters' Home in New York City. He was greeted by the Thing after he returned home from his stint on Battleworld.[390]

Jorgito[]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 2) #91, Punisher (Vol. 2) #92

Jorgito was a member of the elite Bosqueverdan military unit Red Condors.[391] When General Carranza hired them to protect his comfortable "prison" in Sierra Angeles from vigilante Francis Castle, he combed the jungle with his teammates.[392] The Punisher captured Condor Reynardo, tied him to a tree and used him as a bait to make the others reveal their positions, with Reynardo asking for Jorgito's help; Jorgito and Manuel wanted to help a partner in need, but leader Rabio Ramirez ordered them not to. The Punisher then used a trick to attract Jorgito to the jungle, pretending to be in a different position, then when he knew where Jorgito was, he salvoed him.[391]

Jose[]

Appearances: Marvel Team-Up #119

Jose was an orderly and son of the head nurse at the Nursing Home where Aunt May and Nathan Lubensky resided. Josè was paid by Nathan to take him to the old theater where he and Georgie Benny performed as a couple. Arrived at the theater, Josè asked Nathan if it was not the case to go back to the Nursing Home otherwise they would both have trouble, but Nathan told him to accompany him to a hotel, but at the sight of a gang of thugs Josè ran away abandoning Nathan at the mercy of the thugs. He ran to the nursing home and alarmed May of what had happened so she hurried to save Nathan.[393]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man Annual #17

Jose was one of the former students of Midtown High School that attended the Midtown High School's Pre-Reunion Bash.[169]

Appearances: Spider-Man Unlimited #8

Member of the terrorist group Terror Unlimited, he was in charge of the detonator transport but was hit and killed by a diligent security officer.[394]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 10) #5

Jose was Guillermo's driver, who got killed by the Punisher after he let the bomb inside the taxi explode, killing him in the process.[395]

Appearances: Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #1

Jose was a homeless veteran who stood at the corner of the Third and the Bowery, and to whom Peter always gave a little financial help.[396]

Appearances: Champions (Vol. 4) #2

Jose was one of the guys who participated in the march in Chicago against the law that banned underages from being superheroes.[397]

Josef[]

Appearances: Motion Picture Funnies Weekly #1

Josef was a minister of Queen Ursula in European principality Castile D'or. In the late 1930s, he schemed with his queen to start a war with the neighbouring Attania.[398][399]

Appearances: Spy Thrillers #1

Josef was a communist spy who played the double game; in Cairo, he introduced himself to Rick Davis as his informant who pretended to be a communist spy to get hold of documents he would hand over to Rick, but in fact he was a real communist spy trying to appropriate the documents for himself but he was unmasked by Rick who defeated him and thus obtained the documents.[400]

Appearances: Fantastic Four #247

Josef was the burgermeister of Doomstadt and one of the main opponents of the Zorba regime. He rejoiced at Dr. Doom's return to Latveria and made himself available to overthrow the Zorba government and put Doom himself back on the throne.[401]

Appearances: Namor, the Sub-Mariner #51

Josef was a worker on an Oracle oil rig in Louisiana. He says that there had been an accident on the platform but that it had miraculously settled down by herself, not knowing that in fact those who had solved the problem had been Namor.[244]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 6) #19

Josef was the head of a drug traffickers organization that lost a load of cocaine due to the Punisher. Wounded after the assault on the traffickers, the Punisher took refuge on the farm of Joan the Mouse and there confronted him Josef and his henchmen but the Punisher eliminated them all leaving as last Josef slowly killing him with a small Swiss knife.[402]

Joseph[]

Appearances: Captain America: What Price Glory? #2

Joseph was a barman working at the Reef hotel and casino.[403]

Josh[]

Appearances: Spectacular Spider-Man #136

Josh was taking Heloise in full labor to the hospital and was stuck in the traffic jam created following the blackout caused by Electro. Spider-Man intervened and offered to take Heloise to the hospital, but Josh told them he didn't trust to leave his son's safety in his hands, at which point Heloise blurted out telling him to trust and Josh accepted.[404]

Appearances: Spider-Man #75

Josh was a friend of Normie Osborn.[405]

Appearances: Secret Avengers #15

Josh was a reporter for the online tabloid newspaper Unexpected Truth who posted a post fanning the idea that Captain America / Barnes's death was a hoax and this infuriated Black Widow who went to the newsroom and quarreled with the various members.[406]

Joshua[]

Appearances: Jungle Action (Vol. 2) #22

Joshua was a politician who met Caleb in 1867.[407]

Appearances: Iron Man 2.0 #1

Joshua was one of Judith's two children; she had recently been discharged from the hospital but was about to stumble on the stairs where Joshua had left his toys and she asked the kid if he was happy when she was at the hospital getting from him a negative answer and apologizing for leaving toys around.[408]

Josie[]

Appearances: Marvels Project #3

During World War II, Josie was interrogated by the Angel about the Phantom Bullet's death.[409]

Josip[]

Appearances: Punisher: War Zone #35, Punisher: War Zone #36

Josip was a muslim soldier who helped the Punisher, Dragunov and Microchip find the nuclear warhead sold by Viktor Vikady to the Serbian People's Army in Sarajevo.[410]
He helped to find the UN truck used by Vikady to transport the bomb.[411]

Josyane[]

Appearances: West Coast Avengers (Vol. 2) #11, West Coast Avengers (Vol. 2) #26

Josyane was a friend of Bobbi Morse's from her S.H.I.E.L.D. days. Bobbi met her at a beauty salon where she worked as a cover and asked her for information about Nick Fury.[412]
Later, she met her at a pub in Houston to find out if Nick Fury could solve her dilemma, but Josyane replied that Nick Fury was still stuck with internal problems at SHIELD.[187]

Joten[]

Appearances: Red She-Hulk #62

Joten couldn't stop Betty Ross from knocking down Martens in Annapolis.[413]

Joyce[]

Appearances: Zombie #8

Joyce and her group of friends managed to control Simon Garth using his medallion, forcing him to kill their enemies for revenge, including Mambo Layla. Layla, despite being seriously wounded, managed to tear the medallion from Garth's neck freeing him from their control and in full rage Garth killed Joyce and all of her friends.[414]

Appearances: Fantastic Four #227

Joyce ran scared to her husband Edward screaming she saw a winged monster, actually a hawk mutated by a Brain Parasite.[415]

Appearances: Captain Britain (Vol. 2) #4

Joyce and her friend Doreen were walking under a thunderstorm when the monstrous Sidney Crumb appeared on the road, causing confusion among passersby.[416]

Appearances: Firestar #1

Joyce was a regular student at the prestigious and exclusive Massachusetts Academy directed by Emma Frost who crossed her in the school yard with her classmate Peggy.[417]

Appearances: Daredevil #294

Joyce was an activist who, together with Karen Page, tried to get a petition signed against pornography.[418]

Juan[]

[429]
Appearances: Two-Gun Kid #21

Juan lived with his grandad. He helped Kid Colt hide from a bandit, however when the bandit found Colt and threatened to shoot Juan's granddad, Juan killed the bandit.[419]

Appearances: Wild Western #46

With his slingshot, Juan helped Kid Colt defeat Boyle and his gang. The Kid gave Juan the reward for the capture and recovery of the stolen goods that the boy shared with his poor village.[420]

Appearances: X-Men #26

Juan was one of the peasants who heard Kukulcàn's call.[421]

Appearances: Avengers #35

Juan was a rebel who fought against the Avengers when they came to stop the Living Laser; he managed to knock down Captain America, striking him from behind.[422]

Appearances: Iron Man #37

Juan was one of the first to notice the arrival of the Changers.[423]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #292

Juan and Esperanza were a Mexican couple who went with their children to the circus that had arrived in the city. Esperanza asked Juan, since it was the first time a circus had come to the place, if they shouldn't wait, but Juan told her to tell the children that, given their excitement.[424]

Appearances: Incredible Hulk #292

Juan and Miranda were a Mexican couple from a small town. When one evening they saw a being flying in the sky, not knowing it was Dragon Man who had escaped from the Circus of Crime, Miranda, frightened, asked Juan what it was, and Juan, equally frightened, replied that it was a demon.[424]

Appearances: Iron Man #235

Juan was the gardener of Tony Stark's mansion in Los Angeles.[425]

Appearances: Punisher (Vol. 2) #43

Juan was one of Hector Balboa's armed operatives. After Dr. Alonzo Garcia was kidnapped by the Punisher, Juan took part in the motorcycle pursuit guided by the embedded tracker. The chase concluded when the Punisher used the limousine to ram and disable the pursuing riders. Juan was killed in the resulting crash.[426]

Appearances: Punisher Bloodlines #1

Juan was a henchman of Hector Ramone who tried to kill the Punisher by shooting him from a helicopter, but he himself was killed after the helicopter crashed when the Punisher hit the pilot with precision and killed him.[427]

Appearances: Spider-Woman (Vol. 2) #3

Juan accompanied Julia Carpenter's parents and daughter to their lodge in the Amazonian Jungle and there tried to defend them from the Deathweb assault but was killed by Therak's poison.[428]

Appearances: Spider-Man Team-Up #4

Hector and Juan were two Mexican Army soldiers assigned to prevent anyone from approaching the Temple of Tirod, though two local boys attempted to distract them while two American explorers sneaked into the site.[429]

Appearances: Fantastic Four: ¡Isla de la Muerte! #1

Juan was among the festive crowd in San Juan that celebrated Ben Grimm as El Morrito and was recognized by Ben and greeted by him.[430]

Appearances: Moon Knight (Vol. 5) #27

Juan was instructed to hire the Zapata Brothers to do a job for Mr. Alcantara.[431]

Appearances: Daredevil: Dark Nights #7

King forced Juan and his twin sister to duel with swords and after Juan pierced and injured his sister and she cut her hand cleanly, King interrupted the fight and allowed them both to be treated.[432]

Appearances: Squadron Supreme (Vol. 4) #2

Juan met Mark Milton in a diner in Lawton and gave him the inspiration to be a truck driver and be able to travel around the country.[433]

Judge[]

Appearances: Captain America/Iron Man #1

Judge Judge presided over Veronica Eden's plea proceeding. During the proceeding, she poked fun at his surname before cutting to the chase and pleading guilty.[434]

Judith[]

Appearances: Avengers #224

Seeing that her husband Charles did not take his eyes off Janet Van Dyne, Judith sarcastically whispered to her husband to try to keep his eyeballs inside its sockets and he replied that he was just appreciating the feminine aesthetic.[138]

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 3) #10

Judith was a news anchor who interviewed H.A.M.M.E.R. Director Osborn at UBC Studios.[435]

Appearances: Iron Man 2.0 #1

Judith underwent a very dangerous surgical operation, and as they took her to the operating room she asked that nothing should happen to her as she was the mother of two children and their father was not a good person. The operation was successful and she returned to her children but also started building robots in her garage.[408]

Judy[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 5) #49

Judy met Peter Parker at the Metropolitan Museum of Art where the Star of Capistan was being exhibited. She began playing with Peter, quoting Beatles song titles, but when the Star of Capistan took possession of J. Jonah Jameson, Judy was among the visitors to the Museum to be enthralled by the Red Rajah.[436]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 4) #1

Judy was one of the first victims of Hellverine.[437]

Juka[]

Appearances: Venom (Vol. 2) #1

Juka and her mother were fleeing the onslaught of The Bright and their ethnic cleansing when the United Nations Peacekeeping Forces armored troops came to their aid, but it was futile help as all troop members and Juka himself and his mother were killed by Jack O'Lantern.[438]

Jukes[]

Appearances: Tales of Suspense #43

Jukes was the ambitious assistant to scientist Simon Stanley, who disregarded repeated warnings against using the time machine. Driven by a desire for fame and historical glory, he attempted to travel into the past, seeking recognition as the first human to do so. His journey succeeded, but he discovered that the past could not be changed. As a result, he became a ghostly presence, unable to interact with the world, losing his identity despite achieving his goal.[439]

Jukie[]

Appearances: X-Men #111

Jukie was one of the circus workers at "Mr. Mike's One-Ring Traveling Tent Show" in Sullivan County.[440]

Jules[]

Appearances: Ghost Rider Annual (Vol. 2) #1

Jules and her friends were slain by Lucifer in Litwing County.[441]

Julia[]

Appearances: Astonishing X-Men (Vol. 3) #52

Julia was a little girl walking with her mother when she met Warbird, also walking the streets of Manhattan. Warbird noticed the stuffed animal Julia was carrying and commented that it resembled a Skidarian Soul Devil, asking her if she knew how to kill it. Upon hearing this, Julia's mother hurried her away.[442]

Appearances: America Chavez: Made in the USA #2

Julia was America's adoptive cousin, whom she met again when America saved the Washington Heights neighborhood where Julia and her family lived.[443]

Julian[]

Appearances: Marc Spector: Moon Knight #31

Julian was a small kid who ran away from home in the rain one night, after his mum received his bad report card. Moon Knight tracked him down, convincing him a bad report card wasn't the end of the world, and helped him get home.[174]

Julie[]

Appearances: Daredevil #303

Julie was part of a Bronx street gang calling themselves the Die Hards, emulating what was the movie's fashion statement in dirty t-shirts, widows peak haircuts and heavy ordnance. They came to Queens to purchase guns from Nino Cortese, but they couldn't reach a deal and came back home.[444]

Appearances: Alias #15

Julie was a waitress at Christine when Scott Lang and Jessica Jones had their first date there.[445]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man (Vol. 2) #57

Julie was one of Midtown High School's administrative assistants.[446]

Appearances: Deadpool (Vol. 3) #11

Julie was a classmate of Wade Wilson at Surline Elementary School.[447]

Appearances: Uncanny X-Men: First Class #1

Julie was saved by Nightcrawler from falling construction bricks.[448]

Appearances: Magneto: Not a Hero #3

Julie was a news anchor who hosted Christopher Bach to talk about Monica Sims's death.[388]

Julio[]

Appearances: Two-Gun Kid #22

Julio worked for Domino, who was ran out of town by Two-Gun Kid.[449]

Appearances: Marvel Graphic Novel: X-Men: God Loves, Man Kills

Julio was one of a street gang which Kitty Pryde accidentally came across while fleeing from the Purifiers. When Anne appeared moments later, Julio tried to distract her so Martin could kill her with a switchblade, but only wound up wiped out along with the rest of the gang by the Purifier while Kitty managed to escape.[450]

Appearances: Daredevil: The Man Without Fear #4

One of the Kingpin's men, Julio was knocked out by Daredevil.[451]

Appearances: All-New Ghost Rider #1, All-New Ghost Rider #2, All-New Ghost Rider #3, All-New Ghost Rider #4, All-New Ghost Rider #5

Herna was a member of the Blue Krüe gang; he was one of Guero Valdez's friends from Lincoln High School. He helped Guero steal Gabe Reyes' wheelchair only to mock him.[452]
He continued helping Guero with his dealings until the new Ghost Rider gave him and his friends a beating.[453]

Appearances: Marvel's Voices: Community #1

Julio is a friend of Miles Morales. He met Miles when the latter walked into a bodega to buy flags for the Puerto Rican festival, but when the owner of the bodega gave Miles some Dominican flags, Julio corrected the owner telling him that Miles' mother was Puerto Rican.[454]

Appearances: Elektra: Black, White & Blood #2

Julio was a henchman of Cesare , a crime boss of Madripoor. When Cesare went to Joon trying to prevent her from interrupting the pregnancy of whose baby Cesare thought was his son, Cesare ordered Julio to stand guard at the door, but in that while Elektra arrived to help Joon who easily eliminated Julio by killing him.[385]

Juna[]

Appearances: Mighty Valkyries #1

Juna was an Oracle Adventures hostess, assigned as a personal guide to Rūna to accompany her to the interview with the Oracle.[455]

Jung[]

Appearances: Emma Frost #8

Jung was a poker player who managed to beat a desperate Troy Killkelly despite Troy holding sets, which Jung responded with a royal flush.[456]

Junior[]

Appearances: Wolverine (Vol. 7) #10

Junior was a mercenary who worked for Maverick. He was a former member of the US special forces of the Recces of the Seals. With other members of Maverick's Mercs, he extracted Maverick and Wolverine from Madripoor following the clash between the Merchant's forces and the C.I.A.[457]

Justin[]

Appearances: Amazing Spider-Man #252

Justin met Spider-Man while arguing with his girlfriend Weezie.[458]

Appearances: Daredevil (Vol. 3) #7

Justin was one of the kids from the Cresskill School for the Blind who survived the school bus crash during a trip organized by Matt Murdock where they were caught in a blizzard. While walking to safety, Justin asked Matt if he was limping.[46]
